SMTO-CMP-0023 — The AI's final reply doesn't match the reply this task needs

GUID: faa483b0-5d40-4588-af31-8ee119d98538
Slug: completion-output-contract-unresolved
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • The AI wrote a final reply, but it isn't the kind of reply this task needs, such as a written answer or no reply at all. SMTO kept the reply and asked the AI to finish properly.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the task still shows Running, wait. SMTO has asked the AI to finish with the right kind of reply, and it usually does this by itself. The problem is how the AI wrapped up, not the work itself, so it often clears without your help.
  2. If the task stops as Partial · resumable, read the AI's last reply and expand the task to see which steps finished. SMTO kept the reply and the finished steps, so you can see what was done before deciding what to do next.
  3. Send a follow-up message saying whether you want a written answer or no reply, and ask SMTO to check the current result before finishing. A clear request settles which reply is needed, and checking first avoids repeating changes that already happened.

What success looks like

  • The task shows Completed and the final reply you asked for appears in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before asking for it again. Open Technical details, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask the AI to redo any change until you've confirmed it didn't already happen.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Final-response evaluation could not normalize the retained assistant reply into an accepted terminal state, because it does not satisfy the frozen terminal output contract (none or required) or tried to change it.

What this means

  • Final-response normalization cannot produce an eligible terminal state, or retained output-contract parsing prevents accepting the candidate. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • Final-response normalization cannot produce an eligible terminal state, or retained output-contract parsing prevents accepting the candidate.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect retained candidate parse errors and unresolved completion state, not just the message wording.

How to fix it

  • Inspect final_response_candidate.terminal_parse_errors, terminal_output_contract and completion_feedback for the run. The model must finish through finish_task using the frozen contract (a message when required; status completed with no recap when none); the retained answer and receipts are preserved, so do not re-execute work to repair the declaration.
  • Resolve the requested output requirements before declaring completion.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported normalization and evidence checks agree on the intended terminal result.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
